passage: Sunaina read the college handbook twice before saying yes to her first paid job. The rule on page fourteen was clear: students may do paid work outside class hours, provided they declare it to the department. She filled the form the same evening. Samir, whose dad ran a print shop, had asked for a flyer design. Sunaina wrote the price and the delivery date on a small note, kept a folder with every draft, and sent the final file a day early. When Samir found a spelling mistake, she fixed it without charge and said sorry. A week later, two of Samir's neighbours messaged asking for the same designer. Sunaina had not advertised anywhere.

qa.q: On which page of the handbook did Sunaina find the rule?
qa.a: The rule was on page fourteen of the handbook.

qa.q: What did Sunaina feel on being asked by Samir's neighbours?
qa.a: Sunaina was probably pleased and encouraged, since the requests came without any advertising.

qa.q: What could Sunaina do to keep this going, and why?
qa.a: Sunaina could keep the note and folder system for every job, because clear records make later disputes and repeat work easier.

qa.q: How might Samir see the free fix and the early delivery?
qa.a: Samir probably trusts Sunaina and feels well served, which is why the neighbours were told about the designer.

grounding: A student checks campus rules allow paid work, keeps clear records and delivers what was promised, so trust spreads by word of mouth.

passage:
'Simran ma'am, one question before I start anything,' Rukmini said at the warden's office door. 'Can I take paid stitching orders in my room?'
'Hostel rules allow small services. No shop sign, no outsiders coming in. Write it in the register.'
'Done. I'll keep a notebook too. Name, job, price, date.'
Two weeks later her roommate peered at it. 'Why write down every forty-rupee hem?'
'So nobody says I charged them twice.'
'Pallavi's kurta was due Friday. It's Thursday night.'
'Then it's Thursday night.' Rukmini bit off the thread. 'I promised Friday.'
At breakfast on Friday, Pallavi held up the kurta for her whole table.
By Sunday, three girls from Block C had knocked.
'How did you hear?' Rukmini asked.
'Pallavi said you actually give things back on time. And you write everything down.'

qa.q: What does Rukmini write in her notebook for each job?
Why does Rukmini insist on finishing Pallavi's kurta on Thursday night?
qa.a: She is determined to keep her word and feels protective of the trust she is building, even though it is late.

qa.q: What else could help Rukmini's service keep earning trust?
qa.a: Telling each customer a realistic date upfront and agreeing any extra charge before starting, so the notebook and her promises always match.

qa.q: How do the girls from Block C see Rukmini's service?
qa.a: To them it is reliable: Pallavi's word that jobs come back on time and are written down is what brings them to the door. 😊

grounding: Shows a student checking hostel rules, keeping clear records and delivering on time, so trust spreads by word of mouth.

passage:
I'm Omkar, and before I took a single rupee for coding lessons, I went to the department office and asked. The clerk found the circular: seniors could tutor for pay, but not students in any course where they were teaching assistants. That ruled out two juniors who had already asked. It felt annoying then.
Divyansh wasn't in my lab, so he became my first student: four sessions for ₹1,600. After every session I sent him a short message: what we covered, what was left, what was due. When my exams clashed with the fourth session, I told him a week early and held it the next Saturday instead of skipping it.
Next term, Divyansh's roommate messaged me, then two people from his hostel floor. None of them had seen a poster. They had seen my messages on his phone.

qa.q: What did the circular say seniors could not do?
qa.a: Tutor for pay any students in a course where they were teaching assistants.

qa.q: How did Omkar feel when the rule ruled out two juniors?
qa.a: Omkar felt annoyed at the time, since it meant turning away students who had already asked.

qa.q: What would you advise a student starting paid tutoring, based on Omkar's approach?
qa.a: Check the college rules first, send a short written record after each session, and warn clients early when something has to move.

qa.q: How does Divyansh experience the lessons?
qa.a: Divyansh always knows what was covered and what is due, and even a clash is handled early, so trusting Omkar comes easily.

grounding: Shows a student checking the college's rules on paid tutoring, keeping clear records and delivering what was promised, so referrals follow.
